problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${F}^{′}$, the image of $F(2,-2)$ under the action of $T?$

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${S}^{′}$, the image of $S(2,-1)$ under the action of $T?$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $S:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${S}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${S}^{′}(14,-7).$
